title: Bakit May Bill Pa Rin Kahit May Solar?
audience: Homeowners considering or already using grid-connected solar (Meralco franchise area)
premise: Even with solar, a grid-connected home still imports electricity when solar is short or at night, and some bill items remain, so 'automatic zero bill' promises are misleading.

hooks.text: Bakit may bill pa rin kahit may solar na?
May solar ka, pero may Meralco bill ka pa rin?
Zero bill agad kapag nag-solar? Hindi ganoon kasimple.

hookRationale: Direct question mirrors the viewer's real situation, makes no claim of its own and is the approved-direction script's opening.
scriptBasis: Approved-direction script from master spec §11 with V1.1 brand lines substituted (opening 'Hello, SoSmart viewers! Kuya SoLight 'to!', closing signature catchphrase + exact tagline).

cues.text: May solar ka, pero may Meralco bill ka pa rin?
tumutulong ang solar sa daytime electricity use mo.
Pero kapag kulang ang solar generation,
o gabi na at wala kang battery,
puwede ka pa ring kumuha ng kuryente sa grid.
May mga bill charges din na hindi basta nawawala.
Kaya hindi dapat mangako ng automatic zero bill.
Dahil ang gusto ni Kuya SoLight… naka-solar ka na, SoSmart ka pa!

claims.wording: In a typical self-consumption setup, solar helps cover the home's daytime electricity use.
claims.scope: Grid-connected rooftop PV (net-metered or own-use). Generation only while there is daylight; share of load covered depends on system size and load timing.
claims.caveats: Not true for every hour of the day; depends on weather, system size and consumption timing.

onlineCheck.policy: Owner (CHRIS) waived the human technical reviewer for now on 2026-11-24; claims checked online against published Tier-1 data instead.
onlineCheck.note: Consistent with Meralco net-metering page and DOE net-metering programme (system sized to supply daytime consumption).

claims.wording: When solar generation is not enough, or at night without a battery, a grid-connected home still draws electricity from the grid.
claims.scope: Grid-connected systems. Battery-equipped systems may cover some night load depending on usable capacity and configuration.
claims.caveats: Meralco's residential page states the 'not enough' case; night import is stated explicitly on Meralco's DER page (business framing) and follows from PV physics. DOE DC2026-08-0017 release also references grid support when solar is unavailable.

onlineCheck.policy: Owner (CHRIS) waived the human technical reviewer for now on 2026-11-24; claims checked online against published Tier-1 data instead.
onlineCheck.note: Meralco DER page states night import; DOE deck frames net-metering customers as monthly net users of grid power.

claims.wording: Some bill charges do not simply disappear with solar.
claims.scope: Meralco residential billing. Net-metering export credits are valued at the monthly blended generation cost (not one-for-one at retail) and are applied to 'eligible bill charges'.
claims.caveats: Specific peso amounts are not named on screen. The DOE deck is dated 2017, so it confirms the mechanism, not current rates.

onlineCheck.policy: Owner (CHRIS) waived the human technical reviewer for now on 2026-11-24; claims checked online against published Tier-1 data instead.
onlineCheck.note: DOE net-metering deck confirms a PhP/customer/month supply and metering charge applies to net-metered customers, and exports are credited at the blended generation cost rather than the full retail rate, so not every charge is offset. Script stays generic (no peso amounts named).

claims.wording: Installers should not promise an automatic zero bill.
claims.scope: Conclusion from CL-E002-02 and CL-E002-03; also a strict prohibition in the SoLight content policy (spec §8).
claims.caveats: Some months a customer's net bill could be very low; the claim is that zero is not automatic or guaranteed.

onlineCheck.policy: Owner (CHRIS) waived the human technical reviewer for now on 2026-11-24; claims checked online against published Tier-1 data instead.
onlineCheck.note: Follows from CL-03: per-customer charges plus lower export crediting mean a zero bill is not automatic.

caption.main:
May solar ka na, pero may bill ka pa rin? Normal 'yan sa grid-connected setup. Kapag kulang ang solar o gabi na at walang battery, kumukuha ka pa rin ng kuryente sa grid. At may bill charges na hindi basta nawawala. Kaya ingat sa "automatic zero bill" na pangako. ☀️

SoSmart viewers, ano ang solar question n'yo? I-comment lang! 👇
